# Data schemas (generated)

<!-- Generated by `uv run ccil schema docs`; edit the specs in src/ccil/schema/, not this file. -->

## `ccil.trajectories` 1.1

An episode is T frames. Frame t has one entry per observation modality and an action; a transition is (frame t, action t, frame t+1), identified by (episode_id, t) for t <= T-2. Every action frame must be finite because policies also train on the final (observation, action) pair.

### Episode

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `episode_id` | `str` | Unique, non-empty identifier of the episode. |
| `observations` | `dict[str, array]` | Named modalities matching state, state.<name>, or image.<camera>. |
| `actions` | `array` | Action applied at each frame. |
| `terminated` | `bool` | True if the episode ended in a terminal state; False if it was truncated, or if its ending is unknown (termination_known False). |
| `termination_known` | `bool \| None` | Whether the source records why the episode ended (1.1). False: unknown, and terminated must be False; None: not recorded (1.0 files). Set for every episode or for none. |
| `timestamps` | `array \| None` | Frame times; strictly increasing. Given for every episode or none. |
| `task` | `str \| None` | Task identifier or instruction. |
| `action_chunks` | `array \| None` | action_chunks[t, k] is the action intended at frame t + k. Given for every episode or none, with one K. |
| `action_chunk_mask` | `array \| None` | True exactly where t + k < T; required with action_chunks. A chunk never crosses the episode end. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observations[state*]` | float | (T, D) | task-defined | yes | Low-dimensional state per frame; a modality named state or state.<name>. |
| `observations[image*]` | uint8 | (T, H, W, C) | pixel intensity 0-255 | yes | Camera frames per frame; a modality named image.<camera>, C in {1, 3, 4}. |
| `actions` | float | (T, A) | task-defined | yes | Action applied at each frame. |
| `timestamps` | float | (T,) | seconds | no | Frame times; strictly increasing. Given for every episode or none. |
| `action_chunks` | float | (T, K, A) | task-defined | no | action_chunks[t, k] is the action intended at frame t + k. Given for every episode or none, with one K. |
| `action_chunk_mask` | bool | (T, K) | - | no | True exactly where t + k < T; required with action_chunks. A chunk never crosses the episode end. |

Modality names match `^(state|image)(\.[a-z0-9_]+)?$`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `actions`, `episode_ids`, `episode_lengths`, `terminated`, and `obs/<modality>` per modality. Optional: `action_chunk_mask`, `action_chunks`, `task`, `task_present`, `termination_known`, `timestamps`. Per-frame arrays are concatenated across episodes in `episode_ids` order and split by `episode_lengths`.

## `ccil.candidates` 2.3

One row per attempted candidate, accepted or rejected. A row is accepted exactly when it carries no rejection reason; a rejected row may carry several independent reasons. Source identity (episode_id, frame), measurements, and a training weight are required on every row, and the file records the run, seed, generator, input hashes (always including the transition model), and weighting that produced it, so an accepted label can be traced and replayed from the candidate file alone.  Reason columns are the built-in codes, whose meanings are fixed, and namespaced extension codes <namespace>.<reason> that a method's own validators declare (the ccil namespace is reserved). Built-ins come first in their canonical order, then extensions sorted. A consumer that does not know an extension's namespace still treats the row as rejected: accepted is True exactly when no column, built-in or extension, rejects the row.  2.0 made weight, seed, inputs, and weighting required (1.0 had none of them). 2.1 added extension reason codes; a file declares 2.1 only when it uses one, so files with built-in reasons alone stay 2.0. 2.2 added the optional measurement_specs, the definition, norm, and units of every measurement, and the generator's full params; a file declares 2.2 only when it carries specs. 2.3 added optional action chunks (action_chunks, action_chunk_mask, and the meta action_chunk_spec); a file declares 2.3 only when it carries chunks, and lists the arrays in optional_fields so 2.2 readers ignore them.

### Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `str` | Identifier of the run that produced the candidates. |
| `generator` | `dict` | name, version, and params_hash of the generator; optionally params, its full parameters. |
| `seed` | `int` | Seed the generator drew its randomness from. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str]` | SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex) of each input by name; always includes transition_model, the model checkpoint the labels came from. |
| `weighting` | `dict` | name, version, and params of the weighting that produced weight. |
| `measurement_specs` | `dict \| None` | Optional (2.2): for every measurement name, its definition, norm (or null), and units. |
| `action_chunk_spec` | `dict \| None` | Optional (2.3), with action chunks: chunk_size, alignment, guarantee, and truncation; requires the measurement chunk_target_frame. |
| `reason_codes` | `tuple[str]` | Column labels of reasons, distinct and in canonical order: built-ins ['non_finite', 'out_of_support', 'generation_failed', 'action_out_of_bounds'] first, then extension codes <namespace>.<reason> sorted. |
| `observations` | `dict[str, array (N, ...)]` | Candidate observation per modality: a trajectory modality, or latent.<name> for labels in a learned representation. |
| `target_observations` | `dict[str, array (N, ...)]` | Observation the candidate action should reach, per modality. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_episode_id` | str | (N,) | - | yes | Episode the candidate perturbs. |
| `source_frame` | int | (N,) | frames | yes | Transition index t in the source episode (t <= T-2). |
| `actions` | float | (N, A) | task-defined | yes | Candidate action. |
| `accepted` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | True exactly when the row has no rejection reason. |
| `reasons` | bool | (N, R) | - | yes | reasons[i, r] is True when reason_codes[r] rejects row i. |
| `measurements[name]` | float | (N,) | per measurement | yes | Validity measurements (e.g. distance, residual); NaN allowed only on rejected rows. |
| `weight` | float | (N,) | - | yes | Training weight; finite and >= 0 on accepted rows, 0 on rejected rows. |
| `action_chunks` | float | (N, K, A) | task-defined | no | Optional (2.3): position 0 is the label action; position k >= 1 is the source episode's action at chunk_target_frame + k - 1. Only position 0 carries the label's one-step claim. |
| `action_chunk_mask` | bool | (N, K) | - | no | Optional (2.3): True exactly at positions inside the source episode; never padded. |

Candidate modality names match `^(?:(state|image)(\.[a-z0-9_]+)?|latent\.[a-z0-9_]+)$`.

Built-in reason codes: `non_finite`, `out_of_support`, `generation_failed`, `action_out_of_bounds`. Extension codes match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`; reserved namespaces: `ccil`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `accepted`, `actions`, `reasons`, `source_episode_id`, `source_frame`, `weight`, plus `obs/<modality>`, `target/<modality>`, and `meas/<name>`. Optional: `action_chunk_mask`, `action_chunks`. `meta` holds `action_chunk_spec`, `generator`, `inputs`, `measurement_specs`, `reason_codes`, `run_id`, `seed`, `weighting`.

## `ccil.certificates` 2.0

One row per candidate row of a ccil.candidates file, in the same order, with the source identity repeated for joining; the candidates file is never modified. A row records the terms its profile used (every term the descriptor declares is persisted), model_error_value and total_error_value, a classification, is_upper_bound (true exactly for certified, conditional, and calibrated rows), whether the label lies in the profile's neighborhood, and its certificate reasons. The file records the profile descriptor (form, terms, constants with their sources and provenance, the demonstration residual's source, whether model terms are evaluated with an error bound, neighborhood, coordinates and scales, derived units, assumptions), the SHA-256 of every input (always the candidates, dataset, and transition model), and the identity of the representation and transition model.  A certificate is evidence, not a decision: which rows to use is a separate ccil.selection (schema/selection.py), so changing a tolerance never changes a certificate. Version 1.0 also stored an admission policy, a selection, and the admissible and selected masks; 1.0 files are still read, with those legacy fields, and training on them uses candidate.accepted & admissible & selected.

### Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `descriptor` | `dict` | profile, version, form (additive, direct, score), terms {name: {definition, units, required}}, constants {role: {value, source, maps, rationale, provenance}}, neighborhood {state, action} (null = unbounded), coordinates {modality, state_dim, action_dim, state_scale, action_scale}, model_evaluation (bounded: the model terms are upper bounds; assumed_exact: they assume exact evaluation), demonstration {source, value, rationale, provenance} for profiles that add the demonstration residual, units, norms, assumptions. |
| `candidates_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the candidates file. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str]` | SHA-256 of each input by name; always ['candidates', 'dataset', 'transition_model']. |
| `components` | `dict` | representation {kind, version, modality} and transition_model {kind, version}. |
| `classification_codes` | `list[str]` | Exactly ['certified', 'conditional', 'calibrated', 'empirical', 'unsupported']. |
| `reason_codes` | `list[str]` | Exactly ['certificate.unsupported', 'certificate.not_upper_bound']. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_episode_id` | str | (N,) | - | yes | Episode of the candidate row; equals the candidates file's. |
| `source_frame` | int | (N,) | frames | yes | Transition index of the candidate row; equals the candidates file's. |
| `term/<name>` | float | (N,) | per descriptor.terms | yes | Every term the descriptor declares; NaN allowed only where the row is unsupported or the term is not required. |
| `model_error_value` | float | (N,) | error | yes | Additive profiles: the bound on ||f(q) - f_hat(q)||. NaN for direct and score profiles. |
| `total_error_value` | float | (N,) | error | yes | The bound (bound classifications) or score (empirical) on ||T(q) - y||; finite and >= 0 unless unsupported. |
| `classification` | int | (N,) | - | yes | Index into classification_codes. |
| `is_upper_bound` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | True exactly for certified, conditional, and calibrated rows. |
| `in_neighborhood` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | The label lies in the profile's neighborhood. |
| `reasons` | bool | (N, R) | - | yes | reasons[i, r] is True when reason_codes[r] applies to row i. |

Classifications: `certified`, `conditional`, `calibrated`, `empirical`, `unsupported`; bounds: `certified`, `conditional`, `calibrated`. Reason codes, in column order: `certificate.unsupported`, `certificate.not_upper_bound`. Global terms, persisted by every profile: `state_displacement`, `action_displacement`, `anchor_model_error`, `solver_error`. Constant sources: `analytic_bound`, `model_bound`, `declared`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `classification`, `in_neighborhood`, `is_upper_bound`, `model_error_value`, `reasons`, `source_episode_id`, `source_frame`, `total_error_value`, and `term/<name>` for exactly the descriptor's terms. `meta` holds `candidates_sha256`, `components`, `descriptor`, `inputs`, `classification_codes`, and `reason_codes`; no other array or meta field is accepted. A legacy 1.0 file also holds `admissible`, `selected` and, in `meta`, `admission`, `selection`, with the reason codes `certificate.unsupported`, `certificate.not_upper_bound`, `certificate.exceeds_threshold`, `certificate.not_selected`.

## `ccil.selection` 1.1

A selection is the output of one curation policy applied to one candidate set and, optionally, its certificates (#167). It never modifies either: changing a tolerance writes a new selection and leaves both hashes unchanged. One row per candidate row, in the same order, with the source identity repeated for joining.  Per row it records the mask and weight, the raw error the policy compared (the certificate's total_error_value, in the certificate's units), the error-to-tolerance ratio, the relative rank of that error within the named population, and every reason the row was not selected. A ratio of at most one means exactly that the recorded error is within the declared tolerance, which is strictly positive; it is a bound only when the error is (`error.is_bound`). Ranks are relative to the named population of this candidate set, not universal quantities.  evidence_mode is provenance: reference_assisted exactly when reference dynamics computed a constant or residual of the certificate the selection used. evidence_allowed is what the curation run permitted; a data_only allowance never records reference-assisted evidence.  Version 1.1 adds calibration: a selection curated with a ccil.calibration records its SHA-256 and which rows it calibrated. A calibrated row's error is its calibrated bound, a coverage statement at the calibration's level rather than a worst-case bound, so such a selection is always reference_assisted and admits bounds only. Without a calibration a selection is written as 1.0, and 1.0 files are read with no calibrated rows.  A consumer trains on candidate.accepted & mask, with weight.

### Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `policy` | `dict` | admit ['accepted', 'bound', 'score'], tolerance (null or finite > 0, in error.units), quantile (null or in (0, 1]), and population ['admitted', 'produced'] the quantile is taken over. |
| `policy_version` | `str` | Version of the curation rules that produced the selection. |
| `uses` | `list[str]` | Quality terms the policy compares, from ['fidelity', 'novelty']. |
| `caveats` | `list[str]` | What the policy does not establish, e.g. that a fidelity-only policy favours labels close to the demonstrations. |
| `error` | `dict | null` | definition, units, and is_bound of the error column; null without certificates. |
| `threshold` | `float | null` | The error threshold the quantile resolved to; null without a quantile or a population. |
| `evidence_mode` | `str` | ['data_only', 'reference_assisted']: whether reference dynamics shaped the evidence used (provenance). |
| `evidence_allowed` | `str` | ['data_only', 'reference_assisted']: the evidence the curation run permitted; data_only permits no reference-assisted evidence. |
| `candidates_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the candidates file. |
| `certificates_sha256` | `str | null` | SHA-256 of the certificates file; null for admit accepted. |
| `calibration_sha256` | `str | null` | 1.1: SHA-256 of the ccil.calibration used; null or absent without one. |
| `reason_codes` | `list[str]` | Exactly ['selection.not_accepted', 'selection.unsupported', 'selection.not_bound', 'selection.exceeds_tolerance', 'selection.not_selected']. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_episode_id` | str | (N,) | - | yes | Episode of the candidate row; equals the candidates file's. |
| `source_frame` | int | (N,) | frames | yes | Transition index of the candidate row; equals the candidates file's. |
| `mask` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | The row may be used: accepted, and passed every rule of the policy. |
| `weight` | float | (N,) | - | yes | Loss weight: the candidate's weight on selected rows, 0 elsewhere. |
| `error` | float | (N,) | per error.units | yes | The raw error the policy compared: the certificate's total_error_value. NaN without certificates and on unsupported rows. |
| `ratio` | float | (N,) | - | yes | error / tolerance (tolerance > 0); NaN exactly without a tolerance or a finite error. |
| `rank` | float | (N,) | - | yes | Relative rank of error within the named population, in [0, 1] (the fraction of that population with error at most this row's); NaN outside it. |
| `reasons` | bool | (N, R) | - | yes | reasons[i, r] is True when reason_codes[r] applies to row i. |
| `calibrated` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | 1.1, with a calibration: the row's error is its calibrated bound (an eligible empirical row outside the calibration's episodes). Absent in 1.0. |

Reason codes, in column order: `selection.not_accepted`, `selection.unsupported`, `selection.not_bound`, `selection.exceeds_tolerance`, `selection.not_selected`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `error`, `mask`, `rank`, `ratio`, `reasons`, `source_episode_id`, `source_frame`, `weight`. `meta` holds `candidates_sha256`, `caveats`, `certificates_sha256`, `evidence_allowed`, `evidence_mode`, `policy`, `policy_version`, `threshold`, `uses`, `error`, and `reason_codes`; no other array or meta field is accepted. A 1.1 file, written only with a calibration, also holds `calibrated` and, in `meta`, `calibration_sha256`.

## `ccil.diagnosis` 1.0

A JSON document written before generation from the demonstrations, the dynamics evidence, and the configured certificate's declared assumptions. For each recovery length M on the ladder it records five distinct gates, every quantity in the demonstration metric (core/quality.py) with its raw value, quantile, and threshold: - yield: did generation work? the fraction of a fixed probe's labels the   validators accept; - displacement: how far labels move from their sources, q(d_source) / tau_demo; - novelty: whether they reach states the dataset does not already cover,   q(d_demo) / tau_demo, d_demo the distance to the nearest training state; - fit: the held-out M-step model error over the median d_source, from a model   that never saw the held-out episodes; measured at demonstration states, so   necessary but never sufficient; - trust: off-data evidence that the model is credible at the proposed states,   which data alone cannot give: a bound certificate profile whose constants are   declared assumptions or model-computed. The proposed queries' distance from   the training (z, a) pairs is reported beside it. The admitted M is the smallest whose gates all pass (recovery_steps auto), or the declared one (an integer, which skips the ladder but not this report). When none is admitted, the reason names the first failing gate and an actionable next step, and generation writes a valid empty synthetic view.  The diagnosis is data-only evidence: it supports curation and does not establish that the labels improve a downstream policy.

### Fields (JSON)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `evidence_mode` | `str` | Always data_only: no reference dynamics enter the diagnosis. |
| `recovery_steps` | `dict` | requested (auto or an integer), ladder (the lengths probed), and cap. |
| `metric` | `dict` | The demonstration metric: definition, units, per-coordinate scale, and the train and held-out episode and state counts. |
| `timing` | `dict` | dt_ctrl (seconds, or null when the data carry no consistent timing), its source, and a note. |
| `tau_demo` | `dict` | value (null without held-out episodes), quantile, sample (held-out states, and how many were used), and definition. |
| `probe` | `dict` | The fixed probe: the stratification rule, the training episodes and how many it covers, its transitions, and the candidates it produced. |
| `gates` | `list` | Per recovery length: M, horizon_s (M * dt_ctrl, or null), and each of yield, reach, trust with value, raw quantities, threshold, and pass; pass is all three. |
| `admitted` | `int | null` | The admitted recovery length, or null. |
| `admitted_by` | `str | null` | ['gates', 'declared'], or null when nothing is admitted. |
| `reason` | `str | null` | Why nothing is admitted (the first failing gate); null when M is admitted. |
| `next_step` | `str | null` | An actionable next step when nothing is admitted. |
| `bands` | `dict | null` | Accepted probe labels counted by d_demo / tau_demo in the band edges; null without tau_demo. |
| `nested_views` | `list | null` | Recommended labels_per_transition views for a downstream pilot (noisy generators). |
| `evidence_class` | `dict` | The strongest evidence class the configured certificate can give, from data alone. |
| `statement` | `str` | What the diagnosis does not establish. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str]` | SHA-256 of the dataset, split, transition model, and evaluation model. |

A JSON object with exactly these fields plus `schema` and `version`; `statement` is always "data-only evidence supports curation; it does not establish downstream policy improvement".

## `ccil.generate-result` and `ccil.curate-result` 1.0

A JSON document written whole at the end of `ccil generate` or `ccil curate`, in run.output_dir. Each is immutable and named by the SHA-256 of its bytes (generate-<id>.json, curate-<id>.json); generate-result.json is a copy of the latest Generate there. It records the resolved configuration with each value's source, every stage's run directory and whether it was reused, and each artifact's path and SHA-256. Paths are relative to the document's directory and must resolve, through any symlink, inside it: a run directory is a direct child of it. `ccil curate` and `ccil inspect` refuse a result, before writing anything, unless every recorded artifact still has its recorded hash.

### Fields (JSON)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `generated` | `dict` | Curate only: path and sha256 of the generate result it curated. |
| `config` | `dict` | The resolved configuration (ccil.config): each value with its source and units. |
| `stages` | `list` | Each stage: stage name, run_dir (relative), and reused. |
| `artifacts` | `dict` | By name, each with path (relative) and sha256. Generate: ['dataset', 'split', 'transition_model', 'diagnosis', 'candidates', 'certificates'] (split without held-out episodes and certificates without a certificate.profile are absent); Curate: ['calibration', 'selection', 'audit'] (calibration and audit only when configured). |
| `counts` | `dict` | Generate: candidates, accepted, rejected by reason, certificate classifications (or null), and the admitted recovery length (or null). Curate: rows, selected, the policy, its threshold, and the rows not selected by reason. |
| `next_step` | `str` | The command or action to take next. |

A JSON object with exactly these fields plus `schema` and `version`.

## `ccil.calibration` 1.0

A JSON document that bounds the label error, observed under reference dynamics, of one certificate file's eligible rows: accepted rows the certificate classifies empirical. The sampling unit is the episode, since rows of one trajectory, and the labels of one transition, are not independent. Each calibration episode with an eligible row is scored by the largest observed error over its eligible rows; the bound is the k-th smallest of those n scores, k = ceil((n + 1) * level), the split-conformal rule, or null when k > n.  What it guarantees: when the calibration episodes are a random subset of the dataset's episodes, drawn independently of the labels, and the labels and the certificate do not depend on which episodes were drawn (the label model is fitted on every episode: transition_model.fit_episodes all), the expected fraction of the other episodes whose every eligible row has observed error at most the bound is at least level. The probability is over the draw of the calibration episodes; it is not conditional on one draw, a row, or a score. Because it covers every eligible row of an episode at once, it holds for any subset of those rows, including the ones curation selects. It is not a worst-case bound, and it does not transfer to other datasets, tasks, model families, or certificate files.  A row of that certificate file is calibrated exactly when it is eligible, its episode is not a calibration episode, and the bound is not null. Every other row keeps its class.  The observed errors come from reference dynamics, so a calibration is always reference_assisted evidence.

### Fields (JSON)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `evidence_mode` | `str` | Always reference_assisted: the observed errors come from reference dynamics. |
| `method` | `dict` | name and version of the calibration rule (split_conformal_by_episode 1). |
| `level` | `float` | The declared coverage level, in (0, 1). |
| `unit` | `dict` | The exchangeable unit (episode) and its score (the largest observed error over the episode's eligible rows). |
| `certificate` | `dict` | The calibrated certificate's profile, version, and neighborhood; its eligible rows are its accepted, empirical rows. |
| `error` | `dict` | The observed error: definition (||(T(z_G, a_G) - y) / state_scale|| under the reference dynamics) and units, the certificate's. |
| `population` | `dict` | rule, the calibration episodes, and their eligible row count. |
| `bound` | `dict` | n (calibration episodes with an eligible row), k = ceil((n + 1) * level), their scores in increasing order, and value: the k-th score, or null when k > n. |
| `statement` | `str` | What the bound guarantees and does not establish. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str]` | SHA-256 of ['candidates', 'certificates', 'reference']; a calibration applies to that certificate file only. |

A JSON object with exactly these fields plus `schema` and `version`; `statement` is always "when the calibration episodes are drawn at random, independently of the labels, and the labels and certificate do not depend on the draw (transition_model.fit_episodes all), the expected fraction of the dataset's other episodes whose every eligible row has true label error at most the bound is at least the level; the probability is over the draw, not conditional on one draw, a row, or a score, and it holds for any subset of an episode's eligible rows; it is not a worst-case bound, and it does not transfer to other datasets, tasks, model families, or certificate files".

## `ccil.reference-audit` 1.0

A JSON document that compares one selection with the label error observed under reference dynamics, ||(T(z_G, a_G) - y) / state_scale||. It records the observed error of the selected and of the accepted but unselected rows; where the selection's error is a bound, how many selected rows exceed their bound; with a tolerance, how many selected rows are within it; and on calibrated rows, the observed coverage of their calibrated bound, by row and by episode. That coverage is an observation of one draw of the calibration episodes, not evidence for the calibration's guarantee, which is over the draw.  An audit is an annotation, written after the selection: it is never an input to admission, generation, quality evidence, or selection, so a data_only result stays data_only when it is audited (docs/contract.md).

### Fields (JSON)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `selection` | `dict` | The audited selection's policy, evidence_mode, and evidence_allowed, as recorded. |
| `error` | `dict` | definition and units of the observed error. |
| `groups` | `dict` | ['selected', 'accepted_unselected']: rows, and the observed error's median, q90, and max (null without rows). |
| `bounds` | `dict | null` | Where the selection's error is a bound: selected rows, violations (observed error above the recorded bound), and the largest observed-to-bound ratio; null otherwise. |
| `tolerance` | `dict | null` | With a tolerance: its value, and the selected rows whose observed error is within it. |
| `calibrated` | `dict | null` | With a calibration: its level; the calibrated rows (selected or not) and how many the bound covers; their episodes and how many have every calibrated row covered. |
| `statement` | `str` | The audit's role. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str | null]` | SHA-256 of the selection, candidates, certificates (null without), calibration (null without), and reference. |

A JSON object with exactly these fields plus `schema` and `version`; `statement` is always "an annotation of a decided result: it is never an input to admission, generation, quality evidence, or selection".

## Compatibility

Files are written atomically and read with allow_pickle=False. `meta` is a JSON string with schema, version "MAJOR.MINOR", and optional_fields. A file that cannot be decoded (not an archive, truncated, pickled arrays, non-JSON or mistyped meta, inconsistent array layout) raises SchemaError, never a raw decoding error. Compatibility: a minor version only adds optional fields; a reader accepts its own major version, ignores ext/<name> keys, ignores unknown keys only when the file declares them optional (written by a newer minor), and rejects anything else.
